mutations.because: A frame is a fraction of the canvas in [0, 1] (D130), and the domain refuses anything else at both boundaries. Without the clamp a frame of 4 or -0.5 is written into the draft, the saved brief then fails validateTemplate, and the failure surfaces at packaging — far from the number input the user actually touched.

Removing the last element must delete the elements key, not leave an empty list: an add-then-remove would otherwise produce a template a loaded brief never carried, and a brief the user returned to its own starting point would still save as dirty (the round-trip lesson from M3's review).

mutations.after: // mutated: copy on an image element is no longer refused
mutations.because: The domain's field table names no text for the image kind, so an image element carrying copy is refused by validateTemplate. Without the guard the editor writes a key the boundary rejects — the one defect the invariant test exists to catch, because the element looks fine on screen and fails at Save.
